sections.title: Beyond Production: Marxism and Alternative Logics of Value
sections.description: In this seminar we will examine capitalism from the perspective of the production of value. Guided by Karl Marx's Capital, we will examine the processes of the extraction of value from labor, conversion of value into profit, forms of subsumption of labor under capital, and elaborate on the kind of social relations these dynamics produce. We will also learn how capitalist social relations break down previous forms of value and institute new value forms on a global scale. We will seek to extend Marx's analysis and go beyond it in two ways: by investigating alternative forms of value that could be said to persist alongside the capitalist value form; and by interrogating the value extraction in contemporary informatized capitalism that takes place beyond the site of production. For instance, do provision grounds among the enslaved in the 19th century, milpa among indigenous people in the Americas, planned economy and black markets in the Soviet Union, squatting in contemporary urban centers, or networks of mutual care supplement capitalist social relations or oppose them? Or, alternatively, how does contemporary capitalist accumulation appropriate our life-activity beyond the workplace, such as in the reproductive domain, leisure time, education, health, and nature? We will ask whether and how alternative forms of value and its extraction are subsumed by or antagonistic with capitalism. What forms of opposition to the value form can we discern?
